title: Generate in one step, then measure it honestly
brief: Build the shortcut-model loss and the MeanFlow target that let a flow jump from noise to data in one step, then the Fréchet audio distance, its sample-size correction FAD-infinity, and the CLAP score.
hints: In shortcut_target, the second step starts at x_t + d * first, at time t + d, with the same step size d. Reshape d to (B, 1) before multiplying.
In shortcut_loss, build the target row by row with a boolean mask d == 0, and ask the model for step size 2d only on the other rows: torch.where(d == 0, d, 2 * d).
torch.func.jvp(u_fn, (x, s, e), (v, torch.ones_like(s), torch.zeros_like(e))) returns (u, du/ds). The target is v + (e - s)[:, None] * du/ds.
scipy.linalg.sqrtm can return a complex matrix with tiny imaginary parts from rounding. Take .real before the trace.
np.polyfit(1 / N, scores, 1) returns (slope, intercept); the intercept is FAD at 1 / N = 0.
Normalize each row to unit length with np.linalg.norm(..., axis=1, keepdims=True) before the dot products in clap_score.
